name: gower_variable_types
value: ordinal: awara_frequency, age_band, income_band; interval: 1-5 scales, meat meals, max price; nominal: rest

name: pam_k
basis: silhouette; smallest k within 0.02 of best (best k=3)

name: gower_na_handling
basis: about 3% NA per column; no rows dropped, nothing imputed

name: segment_naming
value: rule-based on profile: max student share; then max daily+weekly awara share; then max median max price
basis: names are labels for readability, not validated personas

name: segment_share_in_state
basis: assumes survey sample in each state is representative; n per state 60-200

name: p_choose
basis: binary product vs opt-out; IGNORES competing products, so it overstates take-up

name: choice_shelf_life
value: shelf_life_days_base of fried_seasoned_pack in that state

name: addressable_channel_split
value: population x segment share in state x share of segment that eats awara AND prefers this channel
basis: user decision: volumes are additive across channels (brief formula counted each eater in every channel)

name: soy_missing_fill
value: Uniform(31.4, 434.5) t/100k; default run uses midpoint 232.9
basis: Enugu, Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Rivers: no state-level NASS soy; range = min to 25th pct of 'reported' states (Yobe derived excluded); ASSUMPTION, not data

name: channel_readiness_scaling
value: min-max WITHIN channel (pilot states), then min-max across opportunities
basis: channel units differ (outlets/100k vs 0-1 index); pooled min-max would make street_market dominate; DEVIATION from brief, user decision

name: purchases_per_month
basis: brief; averaged among eaters in segment

name: margin
basis: rests on REPORTED unit-cost totals (3.3-4.7 pts below recomputed); synthetic

name: price_cost_mc
value: triangular(low, base, high) per state; cost = reported_total_unit_cost_*
basis: unit_economics_v1b (synthetic); retail margin held at base

name: coef_mc
basis: covariances ignored; failed/suspect segment models fall back to overall

name: stageA_affordability
value: mean of wealth_index and wealth_upper_share scores
basis: brief gives one 0.4 weight for two criteria
